memoryTip: En-gender: “give birth to” an idea, feeling, or result — cause it.
correctPassage: Poor communication can engender distrust between teams.
wrongPassages: Extra safety checks engendered the risk by stripping every warning label.
They engendered the empty warehouse by hauling every crate out overnight.
Her silence engendered the rumor by answering every question in full.

definition: officially assign a status, role, or name
memoryTip: De-sign it as official — name or assign a role on purpose.
correctPassage: The city will designate several blocks as a historic district.
wrongPassages: He designated the secret hideout by never writing its name anywhere.
She designated the captain by refusing to name anyone at all.
They designated the winner by drawing lots and then ignoring the result.

definition: make an unpleasant feeling less intense
memoryTip: Sounds like “a suage / soothe age of pain” — ease a bad feeling.
correctPassage: A public apology did little to assuage anger over the spill.
wrongPassages: His jokes only assuaged the tension by making everyone angrier.
They assuaged the shortage by shipping even less grain next month.
She assuaged her thirst by locking the water bottle in a drawer.

definition: a made-up falsehood; or the act of manufacturing
memoryTip: Fabricated like fake cloth — a made-up story (or something manufactured).
correctPassage: The diary entry later proved to be a fabrication invented for publicity.
wrongPassages: The live video feed was a fabrication that matched every timestamp on the clock.
Her fabrication of the recipe meant she followed the cookbook word for word.
They called the signed contract a fabrication after both sides had just signed it.

memoryTip: In earnest — sincere, not joking; you really mean it.
correctPassage: In an earnest letter, she asked the board to reconsider the cuts.
wrongPassages: His earnest promise lasted until the door closed and he laughed it off.
She gave an earnest shrug that made clear she did not care at all.
The earnest flyer advertised a free trip, then buried a $900 fee in fine print.
